reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 the RELATIVE KEY phrase's data-name-1 may be written qualified by any Format 1 qualifier sequence of §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 (IN/OF group or record names in successively more inclusive order, gaps allowed, optionally ending in a file-name or cd-name; redundant qualification allowed); the qualified name must resolve to exactly the one item it names, which then is the relative key, and an unqualified nonunique name, a qualifier off the item's hierarchy or out of order, and a subscript on the name or a qualifier are refused.

edition-consulted.switches: a RELATIVE KEY clause not immediately after the ACCESS MODE clause (RelativeKeyClauseAlone2002) is refused below 2002, since the 1985 format makes RELATIVE KEY a phrase of ACCESS MODE; not a qualification switch
EditionInfo.SubscriptedClauseOperands (Year == 2002 only) keeps an integer-literal subscript; 1985 takes the refuse-subscript arm, the same as 2023
Edition.Cite chooses the rule quoted in COBOL2024 (§1985:III.2 p69 at 85); the refusal decision is the same
Edition.CiteRule in the COBOL1639 wording; ReportSection.ReportItemOperandRefused treats a sum counter as a data-name at 85 (kb/Work PB5310), which only affects an operand naming a sum counter
EditionInfo.ConditionNamesShareTheDataNameSet: at 85 a same-spelled condition-name counts against uniqueness (kb/Work PB5972); qualification that reaches the data item alone resolves

reader.edition-search: Read every member on the path from relativeKeyClause to ResolveClauseOperand, DataNameCandidates and QualifierWalk; grepped Edition., SubscriptedClauseOperands, DialectBehaviors, ConditionNamesShareTheDataNameSet and RelativeKeyClause across src. The qualifier walk itself (QualifierWalk, QualifierChainMatchesFrom, FileQualifies, CdQualifies) consults no edition; ClauseOperandsTakeImplicitQualifiers is asked only for data description entry clauses, not file-control clauses.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: qualification of the RELATIVE KEY operand resolves through the same code at 85 and 2023 (r1 and r5 refused identically at --std 2023 apart from the cited rule); the edition arms on the path govern the clause's placement (standalone clause from 2002), a 2002-only subscript, and the 85 condition-name/data-name disjoint set
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise one level of qualification by a level-01 record name (IN in the SELECT, OF in the procedure) with RANDOM and SEQUENTIAL access; not exercised are qualification with a gap over several levels, a file-name or cd-name qualifier, DYNAMIC access, and the refusal half (ambiguous unqualified name, wrong or out-of-order qualifiers, subscripted qualifier)

reader.notes: The RELATIVE KEY operand is captured with its IN/OF qualifiers by DataBinder.KeyReference (through ClauseDataNameSubscripted's shape screen) in FileControlBinder.BindFileControl and resolved post-build by ResolveClauseOperand over the one qualifier walk, which now lives in SymbolTable.DataNameCandidates.cs; every Format 1 qualifier form probed (group gaps, record-name, file-name, cd-name, redundant) resolved to the right item at run time and every refusal form was refused. Side observation, not this rule: each refusal of the key also emits a cascade COBOL0862 on the START ('RELATIVE KEY item (none)'), a second verdict about an operand already refused.
reader.at-2023: r1_ambiguous and r5_subscriptqual refused the same way at --std 2023 (COBOL1639, COBOL2024, citing 2023 rules); p1 and p2 do not compile at 2023 only because LABEL RECORDS is removed there (COBOL0902)

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VIII.2.4.3 SR1 ('Data-name-1 may be qualified.') and §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 (Format 1 and SRL2.1 to SRL2.5, and the scope list item (4), contained programs). Read DataBinder.ResolveClauseOperand (one IdentifyDataName in Model.Scope.Program, survivors counted) and the qualifier walk in SymbolTable.DataNameCandidates.cs; the only edition switch there (ClauseOperandsTakeImplicitQualifiers) is asked only for data description entry clauses, as the reader said. Probes at --std 85 under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/w20262131/coderead/out/refute-1985-c04/runs, each aimed at a form the reader did not try: (c) a_nested_global: SEQUENTIAL access in a nested program, RELATIVE KEY IS RK OF G-REC naming the containing program's GLOBAL record's RK beside a local RK -> 'W 00 G 002 L 777 / OUTER RK 002' (global item updated, local untouched); f_nested_unqualified: unqualified RK in the same shape -> 'W 00 G 000 L 002' (local one by the scope rules, not ambiguous); (e) b_sd_qual: RK IN SORT-FILE, a sort-file-name (level indicator SD) as file-name-1 qualifier -> 'W3 00 / R3 00 THREE / R9 INVALID / R9 23'; (d) d_external: RK OF X-REC, an EXTERNAL record, DYNAMIC access, START and READ NEXT -> 'W1 00 001 000 / W2 00 002 000 / R2 00 TWO / N1 00 ONE 001' (WS RK stays 000); g_record_as_key: data-name-1 itself a level-01 record-name RK in two FDs, RK OF F-TWO (SRL2.5) -> 'W6 00 / R6 00 SIX / R1 INVALID / R1 23'; (b) c_renames_qual: RK OF REN-RK (level-66 RENAMES, not a group RK is subordinate to) -> 'error COBOL1639: ... 'RK' is declared, but not under the given qualifier (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR3 ...)'; e_condname_qual: RK OF IS-ON (a level-88 under RK used as qualifier) -> the same COBOL1639 refusal.
